title: Issue 1: Welcome to MUN Engineering ROAR
excerpt: Introducing the first issue of MUN Engineering ROAR, a student newsletter designed to keep the engineering community informed and engaged.
author: The Engineering Society
content: Welcome to the inaugural issue of MUN Engineering ROAR, a student newsletter created to brighten your day while keeping you informed and engaged with the Faculty of Engineering and Applied Science.
ROAR features faculty updates, student accomplishments, upcoming events, engineering news, and stories from across Memorial University's engineering community.
This first issue reflects on the opening months of the Winter 2026 semester while looking ahead to the exciting events still to come before the end of the term.
Students are encouraged to submit suggestions, stories, and information for future issues by reaching out to the Engineering Student Society.

title: Issue 1: Faculty Updates
excerpt: Icebergs, quantum research, memorable classroom moments, and appreciation for the people behind the first issue.
author: Faculty of Engineering & Applied Science
content: Dr. Stephen Bruneau was featured on CBC's The Nature of Things in an episode titled 'The Berg,' exploring the formation of Greenland icebergs and their journey along Newfoundland and Labrador's coastline.

One memorable classroom quote came during a discussion on the Antoniou Inductor Replacement circuit. When a student asked why so much effort was needed to replace a simple inductor, the professor jokingly replied, 'To make things beautiful — why do you spend an hour in the bathroom every morning?'
The newsletter also highlights Dr. Octavia Dobre's research in quantum computing for communications and networking. Her work focuses on applying quantum entanglement to future communication systems.
Special thanks are given to Dr. Masek, Associate Dean of Engineering and Applied Science, who created the illustrations throughout the issue and contributed much of its written content.

title: Issue 1: Student Team Highlights
excerpt: Engineering design teams continue earning recognition through competitions and innovative projects.
author: The Engineering Society
content: Enactus Memorial competed at the Enactus Atlantic Canada Regional Exposition in Halifax, earning a third-place finish in the Canadian Tire Environmental Sustainability Challenge.
IcebergASV completed another successful RoboBoat competition in Florida, competing against 36 teams from more than ten countries and advancing to the semi-finals.
The MedTech capstone team won the inaugural Atlantic ACL competition with a wearable knee sleeve that combines EMG sensors and motion tracking to support ACL rehabilitation.
Another capstone team, supervised by Dr. Elruby, continues work on an underwater scooter project while overcoming challenges related to sourcing motors and batteries.

title: Issue 1: Engineering Inspiration
excerpt: A blend of engineering humour and timeless scientific wisdom from the first issue of ROAR.
author: The Engineering Society
content: The issue features the famous Archimedes quote, 'Give me a fixed point and I shall move the Earth,' reminding students of the power of engineering principles.
ROAR also celebrates the lighter side of engineering by sharing memorable quotes from classrooms and highlighting the personalities that make the Faculty unique.
The newsletter aims to build community by recognizing achievements, celebrating faculty and student successes, and keeping everyone connected through shared experiences.
Future issues promise additional stories, campus news, engineering updates, and opportunities for students to contribute their own content.
